final_rationale: The verdict does not change because no genuinely new admissible evidence was added. The Actor narrowed the claim and conceded the core defects already identified: the affected enterprise refund workflow remains exposed, rollout controls do not exclude it, the risk acceptance draft is unapproved and does not cover that exposure, and there is no evidence that required pre-launch disclosure has been completed. That narrower framing is more accurate than an overbroad clean-compliance claim, but it is still not enough for compliant_with_caveats here because the caveat is itself an unresolved compliance predicate, not merely a residual risk to document. Under the available policy text, rollout controls and monitoring do not cure the disclosure duty when the affected segment remains exposed without exclusion or approved risk acceptance. The admissible record therefore still supports general launch-readiness evidence, but not evidentially supported compliance for certification on the model-card disclosure issue.
remaining_concerns: The enterprise refund workflow segment remains below target and still exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
Rollout controls are random by workspace and do not exclude the affected use case.
There is no approved risk acceptance covering the exposed enterprise refund workflow segment.
There is no admissible evidence that the required pre-launch disclosure for this named use case was completed.
The actor's narrowed certification theory still depends on caveated future or implied documentation rather than a satisfied policy predicate in the present record.
